extra_prompt: You are booking for a licensed electrical contractor. Ask whether the job is residential or commercial and roughly how old the property is. For burning smells, sparking, scorching, or a safety switch that keeps tripping, tell the caller to switch off the affected circuit at the switchboard only if it is safe, keep away from exposed wires, and treat it as an emergency. Never ask anyone to open a switchboard or touch wiring. Electrical safety certificates for sales or rentals are a separate booking; ask whether one is needed.

kb.q: Are your electricians licensed?
kb.a: Our licence number is [your licence number]. We can send licence and insurance details, including [insurer name], before any work starts.

kb.q: Do you do emergency electrical work?
kb.a: {emergency_note} For sparks, smoke, burning smells, or a power failure to the whole house, call us straight away.

kb.q: What should I do if I smell burning from an outlet?
kb.a: Switch off the circuit at the switchboard only if it is safe to reach it, and unplug anything nearby. Keep away from the outlet, call us, and do not use it again until it has been checked.

kb.q: Why does my breaker keep tripping?
kb.a: A breaker that keeps tripping usually means an overloaded circuit, a faulty appliance, or a fault in the wiring. Do not keep resetting it; book a diagnostic visit so we can find the cause.

kb.q: Can you install a new power point?
kb.a: Yes, we install standard, GFCI, and USB power points, plus dedicated circuits for large appliances. Job time depends on the cabling needed, and we confirm it when we quote.

kb.q: What should I do if a safety switch keeps tripping?
kb.a: Do not keep resetting it, and unplug the appliance you were using. Treat it as urgent and call us, because a safety switch that trips repeatedly needs to be tested.

kb.q: How much does a panel upgrade cost?
kb.a: {price_note} Switchboard upgrades depend on the size of the supply and how hard it is to access. We inspect first and then give you a fixed price.

kb.q: Do you install EV chargers?
kb.a: Yes, we install level 2 home EV chargers and can check whether your switchboard has enough capacity. If panel work is needed, we quote it separately.

kb.q: Do you do electrical safety inspections?
kb.a: Yes, we check the switchboard, safety switches, power points, and visible wiring. You receive a written report of what we found and what needs fixing.

kb.q: Can you install outdoor lighting?
kb.a: Yes, we install garden, security, and flood lighting. Outdoor wiring uses weatherproof fittings and is protected by safety switches.

kb.q: Do you install solar and batteries?
kb.a: Yes, we install solar PV and battery systems. We start with a site survey of your roof and switchboard, then quote based on what we find.

kb.q: How long does a rewire take?
kb.a: The time depends on the size and layout of the home, so we give an estimate after inspection. We discuss staging the work so you can keep living in the home.

kb.q: What does a smoke alarm installation cost?
kb.a: {price_note} The price depends on how many alarms are needed and how the wiring runs. We confirm the number when we visit.

kb.q: Do you work on commercial premises?
kb.a: Yes, we work on retail, office, and light industrial sites, including three-phase supply. Commercial jobs are quoted separately after a site visit.

kb.q: Can you fix an outlet that stopped working?
kb.a: Yes. A dead power point is often a loose connection or a tripped safety switch upstream. We find the fault before we replace anything.

kb.q: Do you offer a warranty on work?
kb.a: {warranty_note} Ask us to explain what is covered before the job starts.

kb.q: What payment methods do you take?
kb.a: We accept cash, card, and bank transfer. Card payments are taken on site when the job is finished.

kb.q: Are weekend appointments available?
kb.a: Saturday morning bookings are usually available. Sunday and public holidays are for emergencies only.

kb.q: Do smoke alarms need to be replaced?
kb.a: Smoke alarm rules vary by state and by the age of the alarm. We check your alarms and tell you what applies to your property and when they should be replaced.

kb.q: How often should my switchboard be checked?
kb.a: Check the switchboard when you buy a home, after renovations, or when breakers run warm, flicker, or trip. Older homes benefit from a check every few years.

kb.q: Can you install an outdoor power point?
kb.a: Yes. Outdoor power points need weatherproof boxes and RCD protection, and we install them to current standards.

kb.q: Do you do pre-purchase electrical inspections?
kb.a: Yes. We inspect the switchboard, visible wiring, power points, and safety switches, then give you a written report before you buy.

kb.q: Can you install ceiling fans and downlights?
kb.a: Yes. We install ceiling fans and downlights, and check the ceiling space for safe wiring and clearances before we start.

kb.q: Do ceiling fans need a new circuit?
kb.a: Sometimes. A fan may need a new circuit or a remote control module, which we confirm on inspection before we quote.

compliance.guidance: Confirm the licence class and registration that cover this work before you quote, and show the licence number where your state requires it. Some work (for example gas, electrical and some plumbing or roofing) must be signed off by a licensed person. Your state regulator sets the rules; check them before relying on this guidance.
